passages.text: Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; so He delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years, and the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel. Because of the Midianites, the Israelites prepared shelters for themselves in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD.
The LORD saw their evil.
The LORD gave the Israelites into the hand of Midian.
This lasted seven years.
Midian became stronger than Israel.
Midian oppressed Israel.
The Israelites feared the Midianites.
The Israelites made shelters for themselves.
They built these shelters in the mountains.
They hid in caves.
They used strongholds for safety.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־ מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃ וַתָּ֥עָז יַד־ מִדְיָ֖ן עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִפְּנֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן עָשֽׂוּ לָהֶ֣ם׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת־ הַמִּנְהָרוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וְאֶת־ הַמְּעָר֖וֹת וְאֶת־ הַמְּצָדֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Whenever the Israelites would plant their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east would come up and invade them, encamping against them as far as Gaza and destroying the produce of the land. They left Israel with no sustenance, neither sheep nor oxen nor donkeys.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites planted crops.
The Midianites came up against them.
The Amalekites also came up against them.
Other people from the east came up against them.
These enemies invaded Israel.
They camped against Israel as far as Gaza.
They destroyed the produce of the land.
They left nothing for Israel to eat.
They took away all the sheep.
They took away all the oxen.
They took away all the donkeys.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֖ה אִם־ זָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעָלָ֨ה מִדְיָ֧ן וַֽעֲמָלֵ֛ק וּבְנֵי־ קֶ֖דֶם וְעָל֥וּ עָלָֽיו׃ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשְׁחִ֙יתוּ֙ אֶת־ יְב֣וּל הָאָ֔רֶץ עַד־ בּוֹאֲךָ֖ עַזָּ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ יַשְׁאִ֤ירוּ מִֽחְיָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֶׂ֥ה וָשׁ֖וֹר וַחֲמֽוֹר׃

passages.text: For the Midianites came with their livestock and their tents like a great swarm of locusts. They and their camels were innumerable, and they entered the land to ravage it.
passages.sermon:
The Midianites came into Israel’s land.
They brought their livestock with them.
They brought their tents with them.
They came in great numbers.
They were as many as a swarm of locusts.
Their camels were too many to count.
No one could number them.
They entered the land.
They came to destroy it.
passages.original: כִּ֡י הֵם֩ וּמִקְנֵיהֶ֨ם יַעֲל֜וּ וְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם יָבֹאוּ כְדֵֽי־ אַרְבֶּה֙ לָרֹ֔ב וְלָהֶ֥ם וְלִגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Israel was greatly impoverished by Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Midianites attacked Israel.
The Midianites made Israel very poor.
The Israelites suffered greatly because of Midian.
The Israelites cried out to the LORD for help.
passages.original: וַיִּדַּ֧ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מְאֹ֖ד מִפְּנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּזְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Now when the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian, He sent them a prophet, who told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites suffered because of Midian.
They cried out to the LORD for help.
The LORD heard them.
The LORD sent a prophet to the Israelites.
The prophet spoke to them.
He said, “This is what the LORD says.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
I am the LORD.
I brought you out of Egypt.
I took you out of the house of slavery.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי־ זָעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה עַ֖ל אֹד֥וֹת מִדְיָֽן׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה אִ֥ישׁ נָבִ֖יא אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּה־ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֣ה׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָנֹכִ֞י הֶעֱלֵ֤יתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וָאֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים׃

passages.text: I delivered you out of the hands of Egypt and all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God reminded them of His actions.
God said, “I saved you from Egypt.
I rescued you from all who oppressed you.
I forced your enemies to leave before you.
I gave you their land.”
passages.original: וָאַצִּ֤ל אֶתְכֶם֙ מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִיַּ֖ד כָּל־ לֹחֲצֵיכֶ֑ם וָאֲגָרֵ֤שׁ אוֹתָם֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם וָאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־ אַרְצָֽם׃

passages.text: And I said to you: ‘I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.’ But you did not obey Me.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke to the Israelites.
The LORD said, "I am the LORD your God."
The LORD told the Israelites not to fear the gods of the Amorites.
The Amorites lived in the land where the Israelites now lived.
The LORD commanded the Israelites not to fear the Amorite gods.
The Israelites did not obey the LORD.
The Israelites did not listen to the LORD's voice.
passages.original: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָכֶ֗ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֤א תִֽירְאוּ֙ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים בְּאַרְצָ֑ם וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּקוֹלִֽי׃פ

passages.text: Then the angel of the LORD came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD came.
The angel sat under the oak tree in Ophrah.
This oak belonged to Joash.
Joash was an Abiezrite.
Gideon was Joash’s son.
Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress.
Gideon did this to hide the wheat from the Midianites.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֞א מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ תַּ֤חַת הָֽאֵלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָפְרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְיוֹאָ֖שׁ אֲבִ֣י הָֽעֶזְרִ֑י וְגִדְע֣וֹן בְּנ֗וֹ חֹבֵ֤ט חִטִּים֙ בַּגַּ֔ת לְהָנִ֖יס מִפְּנֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן׃

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon and said, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon.
The angel spoke to Gideon.
The angel said, “The LORD is with you.”
The angel called Gideon a mighty man of valor.
passages.original: וַיֵּרָ֥א אֵלָ֖יו מַלְּאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו יְהוָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ גִּבּ֥וֹר הֶחָֽיִל׃

passages.text: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all His wonders of which our fathers told us, saying, ‘Has not the LORD brought us up out of Egypt?’ But now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to the angel of the LORD.
Gideon said, "Please, my Lord."
Gideon asked a question.
He said, "If the LORD is with us, why has all this trouble come upon us?"
Gideon asked about God's miracles.
He said, "Where are all the wonders our fathers told us about?"
Gideon remembered the stories of the past.
He said, "They told us, 'Did not the LORD bring us up out of Egypt?'"
Gideon described the present situation.
He said, "But now the LORD has left us."
He said, "The LORD has given us into the hand of Midian."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֤יו גִּדְעוֹן֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְיֵ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְלָ֥מָּה מְצָאַ֖תְנוּ כָּל־ זֹ֑את וְאַיֵּ֣ה כָֽל־ נִפְלְאֹתָ֡יו אֲשֶׁר֩ סִפְּרוּ־ לָ֨נוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֜ינוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲלֹ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ הֶעֱלָ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וְעַתָּה֙ נְטָשָׁ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖נוּ בְּכַף־ מִדְיָֽן׃

passages.text: The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Gideon.
The LORD turned to Gideon.
The LORD said, "Go now."
"Use the strength you have."
"Save Israel from the power of Midian."
"I am the one who is sending you."
passages.original: וַיִּ֤פֶן אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֵ֚ךְ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ זֶ֔ה וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֥ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִכַּ֣ף מִדְיָ֑ן הֲלֹ֖א שְׁלַחְתִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “how can I save Israel? Indeed, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to the Lord.
Gideon said, “Please, my Lord.”
Gideon asked, “How can I save Israel?”
Gideon’s clan belonged to the tribe of Manasseh.
Gideon’s clan was the weakest in Manasseh.
Gideon was the youngest in his father’s house.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔י בַּמָּ֥ה אוֹשִׁ֖יעַ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנֵּ֤ה אַלְפִּי֙ הַדַּ֣ל בִּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וְאָנֹכִ֥י הַצָּעִ֖יר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: “Surely I will be with you,” the LORD replied, “and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Gideon.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, "I will be with you."
You will defeat the Midianites.
You will strike them down as if they were one man.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֶהְיֶ֖ה עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהִכִּיתָ֥ אֶת־ מִדְיָ֖ן כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: Gideon answered, “If I have found favor in Your sight, give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.
passages.sermon: Gideon spoke to the Lord.\r\nGideon said, "If I have found favor in Your eyes, show me a sign."\r\nGideon wanted to know that it was truly God speaking with him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אִם־ נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ לִּי֙ א֔וֹת שָׁאַתָּ֖ה מְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: Please do not depart from this place until I return to You. Let me bring my offering and set it before You.” And the LORD said, “I will stay until you return.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to the LORD.
Gideon asked the LORD to stay in that place.
Gideon said, "Do not leave until I return to You."
Gideon said, "Let me bring my offering and place it before You."
The LORD answered Gideon.
The LORD said, "I will stay until you return."
passages.original: אַל־ נָ֨א תָמֻ֤שׁ מִזֶּה֙ עַד־ בֹּאִ֣י אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהֹֽצֵאתִי֙ אֶת־ מִנְחָתִ֔י וְהִנַּחְתִּ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אָנֹכִ֥י אֵשֵׁ֖ב עַ֥ד שׁוּבֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread and an ephah of flour. He placed the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot and brought them out to present to Him under the oak.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man chosen by God to deliver Israel.
Gideon went into his house.
He prepared a young goat.
He made unleavened bread using an ephah of flour.
He put the meat in a basket.
He put the broth in a pot.
Gideon brought the food out.
He brought it to the angel of the LORD.
He presented the food under the oak tree.
passages.original: וְגִדְע֣וֹן בָּ֗א וַיַּ֤עַשׂ גְּדִֽי־ עִזִּים֙ וְאֵיפַת־ קֶ֣מַח מַצּ֔וֹת הַבָּשָׂר֙ שָׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֔ל וְהַמָּרַ֖ק שָׂ֣ם בַּפָּר֑וּר וַיּוֹצֵ֥א אֵלָ֛יו אֶל־ תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה וַיַּגַּֽשׁ׃ס

passages.text: And the angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And Gideon did so.
passages.sermon:
The angel of God spoke to Gideon.
The angel told Gideon to take the meat and the unleavened bread.
The angel told Gideon to place the meat and the unleavened bread on this rock.
The angel told Gideon to pour out the broth.
Gideon obeyed the angel.
Gideon did everything the angel commanded.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים קַ֣ח אֶת־ הַבָּשָׂ֤ר וְאֶת־ הַמַּצּוֹת֙ וְהַנַּח֙ אֶל־ הַסֶּ֣לַע הַלָּ֔ז וְאֶת־ הַמָּרַ֖ק שְׁפ֑וֹךְ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Then the angel of the LORD extended the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. And fire flared from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. Then the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD stood before Gideon.
The angel held a staff in his hand.
The angel extended the tip of the staff.
The angel touched the meat with the staff.
The angel touched the unleavened bread with the staff.
Fire came out from the rock.
The fire consumed the meat.
The fire consumed the unleavened bread.
The angel of the LORD disappeared from Gideon's sight.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ קְצֵ֤ה הַמִּשְׁעֶ֙נֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָד֔וֹ וַיִּגַּ֥ע בַּבָּשָׂ֖ר וּבַמַּצּ֑וֹת וַתַּ֨עַל הָאֵ֜שׁ מִן־ הַצּ֗וּר וַתֹּ֤אכַל אֶת־ הַבָּשָׂר֙ וְאֶת־ הַמַּצּ֔וֹת וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הָלַ֖ךְ מֵעֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: When Gideon realized that it was the angel of the LORD, he said, “Oh no, Lord GOD! I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man in Israel.
Gideon saw the angel of the LORD.
Gideon realized this was truly the angel of the LORD.
Gideon said, “Oh no, Lord GOD!”
Gideon said, “I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא גִּדְע֔וֹן כִּֽי־ מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה ה֑וּאס וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גִּדְע֗וֹן אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כִּֽי־ עַל־ כֵּ֤ן רָאִ֙יתִי֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה פָּנִ֖ים אֶל־ פָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: But the LORD said to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid, for you will not die.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Gideon.
The LORD said, “Peace be with you.”
The LORD said, “Do not be afraid.”
The LORD said, “You will not die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֧וֹ יְהוָ֛ה שָׁל֥וֹם לְךָ֖ אַל־ תִּירָ֑א לֹ֖א תָּמֽוּת׃

passages.text: So Gideon built an altar to the LORD there and called it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man chosen by God.
Gideon built an altar at that place.
He built the altar for the LORD.
Gideon named the altar “The LORD Is Peace.”
The altar still stands in Ophrah.
Ophrah is the home of the Abiezrites.
The altar remains there to this day.
passages.original: וַיִּבֶן֩ שָׁ֨ם גִּדְע֤וֹן מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָא־ ל֥וֹ יְהוָ֖ה שָׁל֑וֹם עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה עוֹדֶ֕נּוּ בְּעָפְרָ֖ת אֲבִ֥י הָעֶזְרִֽי׃פ

passages.text: On that very night the LORD said to Gideon, “Take your father’s young bull and a second bull seven years old, tear down your father’s altar to Baal, and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Gideon that night.
The LORD gave Gideon a command.
The LORD told Gideon to take his father's young bull.
The LORD also told Gideon to take a second bull that was seven years old.
The LORD told Gideon to tear down his father's altar to Baal.
The LORD told Gideon to cut down the Asherah pole that stood beside the altar.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת־ פַּר־ הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת־ מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֙עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת־ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת׃

passages.text: Then build a proper altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold. And with the wood of the Asherah pole you cut down, take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man chosen by God.
God spoke to Gideon.
God told Gideon to build an altar.
Gideon must build the altar for the LORD his God.
Gideon must build the altar on top of the stronghold.
Gideon must make the altar in the proper way.
Gideon must take the second bull.
Gideon must offer the second bull as a burnt offering.
Gideon must use the wood from the Asherah pole he cut down.
Gideon must burn the offering with this wood.
passages.original: וּבָנִ֨יתָ מִזְבֵּ֜חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עַ֣ל רֹ֧אשׁ הַמָּע֛וֹז הַזֶּ֖ה בַּמַּֽעֲרָכָ֑ה וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת־ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהַעֲלִ֣יתָ עוֹלָ֔ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּכְרֹֽת׃

passages.text: So Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the LORD had told him. But because he was too afraid of his father’s household and the men of the city, he did it by night rather than in the daytime.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man chosen by the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Gideon.
Gideon listened to the LORD.
Gideon took ten of his servants.
Gideon did what the LORD told him to do.
Gideon was afraid of his father’s household.
Gideon was also afraid of the men of the city.
Gideon did not act during the day.
Gideon did these things at night.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת־ בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: When the men of the city got up in the morning, there was Baal’s altar torn down, with the Asherah pole cut down beside it and the second bull offered up on the newly built altar.
passages.sermon:
The men of the city woke up in the morning.
They saw Baal’s altar.
The altar was torn down.
The Asherah pole beside the altar was cut down.
Someone had built a new altar.
The second bull was offered on the new altar.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי׃

passages.text: “Who did this?” they said to one another. And after they had investigated thoroughly, they were told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”
passages.sermon:
The men of the city saw that Baal’s altar was destroyed.
They saw the Asherah pole was cut down.
They saw the second bull was offered on a new altar.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “Who did this?”
They searched for answers.
They investigated the matter.
They found out who was responsible.
They said, “Gideon, the son of Joash, did this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֔הוּ מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽיִּדְרְשׁוּ֙ וַיְבַקְשׁ֔וּ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ גִּדְעוֹן֙ בֶּן־ יוֹאָ֔שׁ עָשָׂ֖ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then the men of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son. He must die, because he has torn down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.”
passages.sermon:
The men of the city spoke to Joash.
They said, “Bring out your son.”
They said, “He must die.”
They said this because Gideon had torn down Baal’s altar.
They said this because Gideon had cut down the Asherah pole beside the altar.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔שׁ הוֹצֵ֥א אֶת־ בִּנְךָ֖ וְיָמֹ֑ת כִּ֤י נָתַץ֙ אֶת־ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְכִ֥י כָרַ֖ת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: But Joash said to all who stood against him, “Are you contending for Baal? Are you trying to save him? Whoever pleads his case will be put to death by morning! If Baal is a god, let him contend for himself with the one who has torn down his altar.”
passages.sermon:
Joash was Gideon's father.
\r\nJoash spoke to all the people who stood against him.
\r\nJoash said, "Are you fighting for Baal?"
\r\nJoash asked, "Are you trying to save Baal?"
\r\nJoash said, "Anyone who argues for Baal will die by morning."
\r\nJoash said, "If Baal is a god, let Baal fight for himself."
\r\nJoash said this because someone tore down Baal's altar.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר־ עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם׀ תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם־ אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד־ הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת־ מִזְבְּחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, that is to say, “Let Baal contend with him,” because he had torn down Baal’s altar.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man from Israel.
On that day, the people gave Gideon a new name.
They called him Jerubbaal.
This name means, “Let Baal contend with him.”
They gave him this name because Gideon tore down Baal’s altar.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא־ ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם־ הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת־ מִזְבְּחֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Then all the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east gathered together, crossed over the Jordan, and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
passages.sermon:
The Midianites were a people who opposed Israel.
The Amalekites were also enemies of Israel.
Other people from the east joined them.
All these groups gathered together.
They crossed over the Jordan River.
They camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מִדְיָ֧ן וַעֲמָלֵ֛ק וּבְנֵי־ קֶ֖דֶם נֶאֶסְפ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֑ו וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעֵ֥מֶק יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

passages.text: So the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, who blew the ram’s horn and rallied the Abiezrites behind him.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a man chosen by God.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon.
Gideon blew a ram’s horn.
The Abiezrites heard the sound.
The Abiezrites gathered and followed Gideon.
passages.original: וְר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה לָבְשָׁ֖ה אֶת־ גִּדְע֑וֹן וַיִּתְקַע֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיִזָּעֵ֥ק אֲבִיעֶ֖זֶר אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: Calling them to arms, Gideon sent messengers throughout Manasseh, as well as Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, so that they came up to meet him.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader chosen by God to save Israel.
Gideon sent messengers through all of Manasseh.
He called the people of Manasseh to follow him.
Gideon also sent messengers to Asher.
He sent messengers to Zebulun.
He sent messengers to Naphtali.
The people from these tribes came up to meet Gideon.
passages.original: וּמַלְאָכִים֙ שָׁלַ֣ח בְּכָל־ מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וַיִזָּעֵ֥ק גַּם־ ה֖וּא אַחֲרָ֑יו וּמַלְאָכִ֣ים שָׁלַ֗ח בְּאָשֵׁ֤ר וּבִזְבֻלוּן֙ וּבְנַפְתָּלִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ לִקְרָאתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Gideon said to God, “If You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said, then behold, I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader in Israel.
God had spoken to Gideon.
God said He would save Israel through Gideon.
Gideon spoke to God.
Gideon said, "If You will save Israel by my hand, as You have said, I will set a fleece of wool on the threshing floor."
Gideon said, "If there is dew only on the fleece, and all the ground is dry, then I will know You will save Israel by my hand, as You have said."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר גִּדְע֖וֹן אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אִם־ יֶשְׁךָ֞ מוֹשִׁ֧יעַ בְּיָדִ֛י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃ הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י מַצִּ֛יג אֶת־ גִּזַּ֥ת הַצֶּ֖מֶר בַּגֹּ֑רֶן אִ֡ם טַל֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה עַֽל־ הַגִּזָּ֜ה לְבַדָּ֗הּ וְעַל־ כָּל־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ חֹ֔רֶב וְיָדַעְתִּ֗י כִּֽי־ תוֹשִׁ֧יעַ בְּיָדִ֛י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃

passages.text: And that is what happened. When Gideon arose the next morning, he squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew—a bowlful of water.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader chosen by God to save Israel.
God promised to save Israel by Gideon's hand.
Gideon asked God for a sign using a fleece of wool.
God did what Gideon asked.
Gideon got up early the next morning.
He took the fleece.
He squeezed the fleece.
Dew came out of the fleece.
He wrung out enough dew to fill a bowl with water.
passages.original: וַיְהִי־ כֵ֕ן וַיַּשְׁכֵּם֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּ֖זַר אֶת־ הַגִּזָּ֑ה וַיִּ֤מֶץ טַל֙ מִן־ הַגִּזָּ֔ה מְל֥וֹא הַסֵּ֖פֶל מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not be angry with me; let me speak one more time. Please allow me one more test with the fleece. This time let it be dry, and the ground covered with dew.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to God.
Gideon was a leader chosen by God to save Israel.
Gideon said, "Do not be angry with me."
Gideon asked God to let him speak again.
Gideon said, "Let me test once more with the fleece."
Gideon asked, "Let the fleece be dry only."
Gideon said, "Let there be dew on all the ground."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר גִּדְעוֹן֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל־ יִ֤חַר אַפְּךָ֙ בִּ֔י וַאֲדַבְּרָ֖ה אַ֣ךְ הַפָּ֑עַם אֲנַסֶּ֤ה נָּא־ רַק־ הַפַּ֙עַם֙ בַּגִּזָּ֔ה יְהִי־ נָ֨א חֹ֤רֶב אֶל־ הַגִּזָּה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ וְעַל־ כָּל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ יִֽהְיֶה־ טָּֽל׃

passages.text: And that night God did so. Only the fleece was dry, and dew covered the ground.
passages.sermon:
God acted that night.
God did what Gideon asked.
The fleece was dry.
Dew covered all the ground.
Only the fleece was dry.
The ground was wet with dew.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ אֱלֹהִ֛ים כֵּ֖ן בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיְהִי־ חֹ֤רֶב אֶל־ הַגִּזָּה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ וְעַל־ כָּל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ הָ֥יָה טָֽל׃פ
